Preview P6 budgets (issue #170, docs/design/reference-equantic-ui.md section 7.4; ADR-045 consequences). Checked by scripts/check_preview_budget.py. TWO-SIDED RATCHET: an entry fails when it is worse than its budget by more than tolerance.worse, AND when it is better by more than tolerance.better (the budget went stale and must be tightened with --update, which never loosens any entry). The two sides carry different percentages on purpose: a single symmetric band wide enough for a noisy timing row (300%) would make the lower bound negative and silently disable the staleness side, so 'better' stays under 100% for every entry. Only download_gzip_bytes is ENFORCED: it is exactly reproducible for a fixed input and zlib build, so its 5%/1% band is measurement slack, not noise cover, and it is the number the slice's acceptance is about. The two latency entries WARN, for two separate reasons. (1) They are the ENGINE'S SHARE ONLY: cold time-to-first-frame also needs the browser's HTML/CSS parse and a WebGPU frame (P3, not landed), and edit-to-view needs that frame too. They are named for what was measured instead of borrowing the slice's name for a number that is not the whole path; the browser lane adds cold_first_frame_ms/edit_to_view_ms beside them. (2) Wall-clock time on a shared CI runner is not reproducible (docs/guides/testing.md section 7). Their mitigations are tolerance.worse = 300% (a multiple, so only an order-of-magnitude change fires) and min-over-N-fresh-processes, which discards contention instead of averaging it in. Their tolerance.better is a plain 20%: the min statistic is already close to the true cost, so a 20% improvement is real news and worth recording. OWNER DECISION 2026-11-18 (issue #391): download_gzip_bytes is PINNED AT 10 MB (10000000) with tolerance.better 80%/worse 5% UNTIL THE STUDIO SETTLES, because the studio ships several times a day and each slice moved the number by about 0.1% and cost a CI round trip (#508, #511, #513, #515). source.module: tessera_diagnostics_wasm, the P1 page module (src/compiler/codegen/CMakeLists.txt); the same bytes the Pages lane assembles into build/pages. Its two files (the loader and the wasm) are measured from the module directory, not from dist/: they are linked engine artifacts copied next to the page, never bundled
source.page: the built page, designer/web/dist/ (issue #422, ADR-054 decision 6). The measurement walks that directory rather than naming files: Vite emits content-hashed assets (assets/index-<hash>.js, assets/index-<hash>.css) that a fixed list cannot name, and walking the directory keeps the rule the old PAGE_FILES list existed for -- an asset that ships is an asset that is weighed -- true by construction. The tree is index.html (the mount point), the hashed JS and CSS chunks (React 19 chrome plus the three view sessions), the two pre-merge redirect stubs, redirect.js and samples.json, which Vite copies from designer/web/public/. The three Wasm loaders are not in the bundle: they are lazy import()s the Pages lane copies next to the page, and only tessera_diagnostics is weighed because it is the one on the first-paint path
source.runtime: the module runs in the Emscripten Node host ($EMSDK_NODE in CI); a browser host cannot be measured in this lane

download_gzip_bytes.measures: gzip-9 bytes of the whole designer/web/ page directory plus tessera_diagnostics.js + tessera_diagnostics.wasm: the transfer a browser pays for the page and its module

cold_engine_ready_ms.measures: minimum over 5 fresh processes of (module instantiation + first compile); the engine's share of cold time-to-first-frame, NOT the frame

edit_compile_ms.measures: minimum over 5 fresh processes of the per-edit minimum compile of 30 edits after 5 warm-up compiles; the engine's share of edit-to-view, NOT the frame
